data: The course is intended for second year undergraduate students and is meant to be an introduction to the physical and chemical principles that underlie and underpin the biology of organisms. The course will help students understand the molecular logic of life; it will enable them to find answers to questions pertaining to the various aspects of a biological system; these are some samples. How, in biological systems, is energy created or captured, stored, and transmuted, and how is the need for energy sensed? What are the energetic and kinetic bases of a biochemical reaction, which is in turn a unit of a physiological process? How are the various biomolecules synthesized and degraded, and how is the balance between anabolism and catabolism maintained? What are the guiding principles of this homeostasis? How are the various physiological processes orchestrated and synchronized at the level of the system? How does a bodily fluid such as blood act as a buffer, and how is this physiologically important? What are the various classes of biomolecules that make up molecular superstructures, and how do their structures help them perform their function? Instruction in the above will help the student to begin to learn to interpret experimental data, and to better understand biochemical research.
